engine_gap.behavior: Deliver a durable, deduplicated, at-least-once (idempotent) notification of a Work's needs_input/blocked/failed/done transitions to a registered external consumer profile, retried on a durable backoff schedule, independent of any Work's own process/session lifetime, and gate that Work's terminal cleanup on delivery being acknowledged or explicitly retired.
engine_gap.source_evidence: docs/callbacks.md's whole retry/recovery and cleanup-gate sections: state.json tracks pending/delivering/acknowledged/rejected with attempt count and backoff independent of the originating fleet task's own process; `sgt-callback drain --all` runs as a session-independent periodic drain; `sgt-cleanup` refuses full deletion until `sgt-callback check-acked` succeeds.
lower_rungs_attempted: Represent delivery as a stage inside the originating Work's own workflow (§6.3)
Represent delivery as a helper script an actor stage invokes when the Work's state changes (§6.5)
Represent the retry/backoff schedule as workflow-local or shared context data read by a stage (§6.6)
why_each_fails: A stage inside the originating Work's workflow ends when that Work's execution ends; but acknowledgement, retry, and the cleanup-blocking gate must all keep functioning after the Work's own process (and even its own execution context) is gone, including across daemon restarts.

A helper invoked at one state transition cannot express a periodic, session-independent drain across every pending event for every Work in the fleet, nor a durable claim/backoff state that must be safe under concurrent drains.

Shared context can hold static configuration (profile names, timeouts) but not the per-event mutable state machine (claimed, stale-claim recovery after 60s, exponential backoff, terminal seal) that must be read and written safely from a process wholly separate from the Work that created the event.
engine_gap.minimum_runtime_capability_required: The runtime must own a durable, versioned outbound-notification queue (keyed by Work + correlation id + generation) with idempotent enqueue, an independently schedulable drain/retry primitive that is not bound to any single Work's lifetime, and an explicit terminal-seal/acknowledgement gate that a Work's own cleanup path can query without the Work's own execution context still existing.
engine_gap.observable_acceptance_test: Given a Work reaches a terminal state while no coordinator or worker process is attached, and the daemon restarts between the state change and successful external delivery, the registered consumer still receives exactly one delivery (retried per backoff on transient failure) and the Work's cleanup is blocked until that delivery is acknowledged or an operator explicitly retires it.
